title: Amy Williams dies
place: Kitchen of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough

cast.A_MARY: Amy Williams, widow of John Williams of Great House farm, aged 65
cast.B_JOHN: John Williams, who has farmed Great House since 1855 (most likely her son; inferred)

shots.direction: Date-and-place card. Winter dusk, 23 December 1864. The whitewashed farmhouse and yard of Great House sit on the inland hill at Llandough. Frost lies on the yard and one window glows with firelight. Beyond and below, the Ely winds through grey marshes toward a distant estuary haze. There is no coastline at the farm. Slow push in toward the lit window.

shots.direction: Inside the kitchen by candle and firelight. Flagstones, an oak dresser with plates, and a low peat-and-coal fire in the inglenook. A box bed stands by the hearth, where a dying person would most likely be brought for warmth. Amy lies propped on pillows. On the dresser, beside the candlestick, a folded farm schedule and an account book hint at the fields she has known. Slow lateral drift past the dresser toward the bed. Ambience only: fire, wind at the window, a clock ticking.

1842: tithe plan and apportionment for Llandough-juxta-Penarth (Glamorgan Archives P35) (CH-0012)

shots.direction: Medium two-shot at the bedside. Gwen sits on a stool in a dark wool shawl, holding Amy's hand. Her spectacles hang on a ribbon at her chest. She looks up at John, who stands by the fire, and speaks low so as not to wake Amy.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (Glamorgan), soft and low; native review needed
lines.cy: Ma' hi'n gwanhau, John. Ma' 'i dwylo hi'n o'r, er gwaetha'r tân.
lines.en: She's weakening, John. Her hands are cold, for all the fire.
lines.es: Se está apagando, John. Tiene las manos frías, a pesar del fuego.

shots.direction: Close shot of Amy on the pillow, grey hair loose from its bun. Her eyes open as John kneels and takes her other hand. She speaks to him faintly, with effort.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close shot, 1864, an elderly Welsh woman aged about 65 lying on white linen pillows in a wooden box bed, grey hair partly loosened from a bun, strong cheekbones, grey-green eyes, a small mole on her left cheek, pale and frail, a heavy weathered male hand holding hers in the foreground, warm firelight on one side of her face, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (Glamorgan), elderly and faint; native review needed
lines.cy: John bach… paid â gadel i'r tân fynd mas. Ddim dros y Nadolig. Ma'r caeau yn dy ddwylo di nawr, fel o'n nhw yn nwylo dy dad.
lines.en: John, bach… don't let the fire go out. Not over Christmas. The fields are in your hands now, as they were in your father's.
lines.es: John, querido… no dejés que se apague el fuego. No en Navidad. Los campos están en tus manos ahora, como estuvieron en las de tu padre.

shots.direction: Wide, still. Amy's breathing stops. John stays kneeling with his head bowed over her hand. Gwen rises slowly and lays the blanket straight. The clock ticks on and the fire settles. Very slow pull back. Ambience only.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 still, 1864 Welsh farmhouse kitchen at night, wide view, a broad-faced farmer in his forties with a grey-flecked beard and heavy hands, in a waistcoat and shirtsleeves, kneeling with his head bowed beside a box bed where an elderly woman lies at peace, an older neighbour woman in a shawl standing and smoothing the blanket, the inglenook fire low, a longcase clock in shadow, candle guttering, solemn stillness, no text, no heraldry

captions.text: 23 Dec 1864: Amy Williams, "relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm", dies at Llandough, aged 65 (CH-0014)

shots.direction: Medium close on John as he stands, still holding his mother's hand, and speaks quietly to Gwen.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close, 1864, a weathered Welsh farmer in his forties with a broad face and grey-flecked beard, wearing a collarless shirt and dark waistcoat, standing beside a box bed in a firelit farmhouse kitchen, eyes wet, holding an old woman's hand, bare head, warm amber light, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (Glamorgan), quiet and steady; native review needed
lines.cy: Ma' hi wedi mynd, Gwen. Chwe deg pump o'dd hi. Hi gadwodd y gegin 'ma, bob gaea'.
lines.en: She's gone, Gwen. Sixty-five, she was. She kept this kitchen, every winter.
lines.es: Se fue, Gwen. Tenía sesenta y cinco años. Ella sostuvo esta cocina, invierno tras invierno.

shots.direction: Gwen at the dresser lifts the candle and puts on her spectacles, practical in grief. She speaks to John. Who sent the death notice is not known. Here it is shown as a neighbour's offer, the most likely kind of moment.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, 1864 Welsh farmhouse kitchen, a round-faced woman in her sixties with silver curls and rosy cheeks, in a dark shawl, putting on small wire spectacles beside an oak dresser while holding a brass candlestick, her expression resolute and tender, firelight behind, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (Glamorgan); English words of the notice spoken with a Welsh accent; native review needed
lines.cy: Fe sgrifenna i at y Cardiff Times. 'Relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm.' Fel 'na ddyle fe fod yn y papur, John.
lines.en: I'll write to the Cardiff Times. 'Relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm.' That's how it should stand in the paper, John.
lines.es: Le voy a escribir al Cardiff Times. «Viuda del finado señor John Williams, granja Great House». Así tiene que salir en el diario, John.

shots.direction: John turns from the bed toward the small window, his face lit by the fire, and answers her.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close, 1864, a bearded Welsh farmer in his forties in a dark waistcoat turning toward a small-paned farmhouse window, frost on the glass, firelight on half his face and cold blue night beyond, a grave and tired expression, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (Glamorgan); native review needed
lines.cy: Diolch, Gwen. Fe a' i at y ficer bore fory.
lines.en: Thank you, Gwen. I'll go to the vicar first thing tomorrow.
lines.es: Gracias, Gwen. Mañana temprano voy a ver al vicario.

shots.direction: From the farmhouse window, the frozen fields of Great House fall away in moonlight toward the Ely marshes, with Leckwith woods dark across the valley. The view is inland, with no sea. Slow pan across the hedged fields. Ambience: wind, a distant dog.

captions.text: 1855: John Williams succeeds his father in the occupancy of the farm, as reported in the Cardiff Times, 16 Jul 1904, which calls him "of Llandough Farm". That he is the Great House John Williams is an inference (CH-0013)

shots.direction: Closing still. Gwen draws the curtain across the window, and the kitchen holds only the low fire and one candle by the box bed. Slow fade.

continuity: From the curtained kitchen at Great House, cut to the vestry of the new church, where John Williams, now the farm's sole occupier, waits his turn as the assistant overseer enters him in the poor rate for the glebe land.
